edges.description: The mutant protein is proposed to act by disabling the wild-type protein it dimerizes with.
One consequence of impaired TRAF7 function is loss of an interaction required to maintain cilia.
edges.target: Disrupted TRAF7-IFT57 interaction and ciliary loss

edges.description: Mutant TRAF7 changes the output of the MAP kinase module it scaffolds.
edges.target: Altered ERK1/2 signalling in patient-derived cells

edges.description: Ciliary signalling is required in the neural crest lineage that gives rise to the affected craniofacial and outflow-tract structures.
edges.source: Disrupted TRAF7-IFT57 interaction and ciliary loss

edges.description: Altered signalling output is reflected in the transcriptome of patient cells.
edges.source: Altered ERK1/2 signalling in patient-derived cells

edges.description: Developmental gene dysregulation converges on the same affected lineages.
Outflow-tract and ductal lesions follow from disturbed neural-crest contribution to the developing heart.
The recognizable gestalt reflects the craniofacial neural-crest derivatives.
Premature suture fusion in a reported subgroup, involving neural-crest-derived calvarial bone.
Developmental delay is the most consistent feature but has no demonstrated route from the neural-crest argument; the link is recorded as unknown.
Digital anomalies are a core feature; the developmental route to them is not established.
The null mouse establishes that TRAF7 is required for endothelial integrity through the MEKK3-MEK5-ERK5-KLF2 axis, but it does not model this disease's lesion.
edges.limitations: Complete loss of Traf7 is embryonic lethal in mouse, whereas humans heterozygous for a TRAF7 missense allele survive with a congenital-anomaly syndrome. The model therefore tests loss of function, which is the mechanism the human variant pattern argues against, and its severity is not comparable. No heterozygous knock-in of a recurrent human CAFDADD allele has been reported, so the dominant-negative mechanism modelled in this entry has no mouse model at all.

nodes.description: Digital deviations are one of the three organ systems in the disease name. Brachydactyly and syndactyly are also reported.

evidence.reference_title: De Novo Missense Variants in TRAF7 Cause Developmental Delay, Congenital Anomalies, and Dysmorphic Features.
evidence.snippet: The seven individuals share substantial phenotypic overlap, with developmental delay, congenital heart defects, limb and digital anomalies, and dysmorphic features emerging as key unifying features.

nodes.description: A recognizable gestalt in which blepharophimosis is the most characteristic element, with arched eyebrows also noted. Ptosis, hypertelorism and ear and nose anomalies are described in the cohorts.

evidence.reference_title: Phenotypic spectrum and transcriptomic profile associated with germline variants in TRAF7.
evidence.snippet: Major features include a recognizable facial gestalt (characterized in particular by blepharophimosis), short neck, pectus carinatum, digital deviations, and patent ductus arteriosus.

evidence.reference_title: Expanding the Phenotypic Spectrum of TRAF7-Related Cardiac, Facial, and Digital Anomalies With Developmental Delay: Report of 11 New Cases and Literature Review.
evidence.snippet: Facial features, including arched eyebrows, contribute to the distinct gestalt.

nodes.description: TRAF7 sits on MAP kinase signalling. In vitro, the mutations observed in the discovery series reduced ERK1/2 phosphorylation. Note this is not simply reduced TRAF7 activity read forward: wild-type TRAF7 inhibits MEK1/2, so naive loss of function would be expected to raise rather than lower ERK output. The direction of the measured effect is recorded here; its reconciliation with the pathway topology is not asserted.
nodes.id: Altered ERK1/2 signalling in patient-derived cells

evidence.reference_title: De Novo Missense Variants in TRAF7 Cause Developmental Delay, Congenital Anomalies, and Dysmorphic Features.
evidence.snippet: In vitro analyses of the observed TRAF7 mutations showed reduced ERK1/2 phosphorylation.

evidence.reference_title: TRAF7 in signaling and disease: emerging mechanisms and clinical implications.
evidence.snippet: It is an E3 ubiquitin ligase that activates MEKK3 and KLF2/4 signaling, inhibits MEK1/2 and c-Myb along with an NF-κβ-modulator, and stabilizes VE-cadherins in cell junctions.

nodes.description: Congenital heart disease is a major source of early morbidity. Patent ductus arteriosus is the single most frequent lesion, followed by septal and valvular defects.

evidence.reference_title: The spectrum of heart defects in the TRAF7-related multiple congenital anomalies-intellectual disability syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Patent ductus arteriosus (PDA; not found in Mishra-Gorur et al.’s patients) is the most frequent feature, followed by septal and valvular defects.

evidence.reference_title: Expanding the Phenotypic Spectrum of TRAF7-Related Cardiac, Facial, and Digital Anomalies With Developmental Delay: Report of 11 New Cases and Literature Review.
evidence.snippet: Cardiac defects, frequently severe, pose early-life complications.

nodes.description: A severe cranial subgroup has been described with multi-suture craniosynostosis, a pear-shaped skull, sinus pericranii and craniocervical junction anomalies. It is reported in a minority of patients and is not a core feature.

evidence.reference_title: Sinus pericranii, skull defects, and structural brain anomalies in TRAF7-related disorder.
evidence.snippet: In addition to the typical hallmarks of the TRAF7-related disorder, both subjects presented with a recognizable "pear-shaped" skull due to multiple craniosynostosis, sinus pericranii, skull base/cranio-cervical junction anomalies, dysgyria, and inferior cerebellar vermis hypoplasia.

evidence.reference_title: Multi-suture craniosynostosis in c.1570C>T (p.Arg524Trp) mutated TRAF7: a case report.
evidence.snippet: Here, we report a child who presented with multi-suture craniosynostosis and had the uncommon c.1570C>T (p.Arg524Trp) variant of TRAF7.

nodes.description: Both germline and somatic TRAF7 mutants disrupt the interaction between TRAF7 and the intraflagellar transport protein IFT57, and cilia degrade. Knockdown of TRAF7 in Xenopus and zebrafish produces cardiac, craniofacial and ciliary defects, so the pathway is at least sufficient to generate the organ systems involved in this syndrome.
nodes.id: Disrupted TRAF7-IFT57 interaction and ciliary loss

evidence.reference_title: Pleiotropic role of TRAF7 in skull-base meningiomas and congenital heart disease.
evidence.snippet: Somatic and inherited mutations disrupt TRAF7-IFT57 interactions leading to cilia degradation.

evidence.reference_title: Pleiotropic role of TRAF7 in skull-base meningiomas and congenital heart disease.
evidence.snippet: TRAF7-mutant meningioma primary cultures lack cilia, and TRAF7 knockdown causes cardiac, craniofacial, and ciliary defects in Xenopus and zebrafish, suggesting a mechanistic convergence for TRAF7-driven meningiomas and developmental heart defects.

nodes.description: Mutant TRAF7 heterodimerizes with wild-type TRAF7 and inhibits its function. Independently, disease-causing substitutions in the coiled-coil region impair formation of the TRAF7 coiled-coil trimer, which gives a structural route to the same outcome for the subset of alleles that are not in the WD40 repeats.

animal_models.description: The null mouse establishes that TRAF7 is required for endothelial integrity through the MEKK3-MEK5-ERK5-KLF2 axis, but it does not model this disease's lesion.
animal_models.genotype: Traf7 germline and endothelial conditional knockout
animal_models.name: Traf7 knockout mouse

evidence.reference_title: Pleiotropic role of TRAF7 in skull-base meningiomas and congenital heart disease.
evidence.snippet: We show that TRAF7 mutants operate in a dominant manner, inhibiting protein function via heterodimerization with wild-type protein.

evidence.reference_title: The structure of TRAF7 coiled-coil trimer provides insight into its function in zebrafish embryonic development.
evidence.snippet: Additionally, disease-causing mutations in TRAF7 CC region could impair the trimer formation, consequently impacting early embryonic development of zebrafish.

nodes.description: Whole-transcriptome sequencing of patient fibroblasts against controls identified differentially expressed genes. The reported theme is dysregulation of human developmental genes, with enrichment for axon guidance, Wnt/calcium signalling and cardiac hypertrophy pathways. The individual pathway enrichments have not been followed up functionally and are recorded as a described result rather than as established mechanism.

evidence.reference_title: Phenotypic spectrum and transcriptomic profile associated with germline variants in TRAF7.
evidence.snippet: Several differentially expressed genes were identified in patient fibroblasts.

evidence.reference_title: TRAF7 in signaling and disease: emerging mechanisms and clinical implications.
evidence.snippet: Of 76 differentially expressed genes identified in TRAF7 syndrome patients, the main theme identified was dysregulation of human developmental genes, including FLNB, IGFBP7, NOTCH3, BCL2, and PTGS2

nodes.description: A heterozygous germline missense substitution, most often in one of the seven C-terminal WD40 repeats. p.Arg655Gln, p.Arg524Trp and p.Phe617Leu are the recurrent alleles. The clustering and recurrence, and the near-absence of truncating alleles in this syndrome, are the reasons haploinsufficiency is not the favoured mechanism.

evidence.reference_title: TRAF7 in signaling and disease: emerging mechanisms and clinical implications.
evidence.snippet: TRAF7 syndrome is caused by several pathogenic TRAF7 mutations, most of which are located within the WD40 repeat protein domain, and the most recurrent of these mutations are p.Arg655Gln, p.Arg524Trp, and p.Phe617Leu

evidence.reference_title: The spectrum of heart defects in the TRAF7-related multiple congenital anomalies-intellectual disability syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Variants are predominantly within the WD40 repeats and recurrent, suggesting specific alterations to the protein as the pathomechanism, as opposed to haploinsufficiency.

genetic_context.description: DOMINANT_NEGATIVE is used because two independent sources state that the mutant protein interferes with the wild-type protein by heterodimerizing with it, and because the variant pattern argues against loss of function. Note this is the leading model rather than a settled fact, and the mechanism may differ by allele.

nodes.description: Developmental delay, particularly of motor and expressive-language milestones, is the most consistent feature. Severity varies widely, and the 2024 series reported individuals whose early psychomotor delay resolved into normal development, so delay should not be treated as an obligate criterion despite appearing in the disease name.

evidence.reference_title: De Novo Missense Variants in TRAF7 Cause Developmental Delay, Congenital Anomalies, and Dysmorphic Features.
evidence.snippet: The seven individuals share substantial phenotypic overlap, with developmental delay, congenital heart defects, limb and digital anomalies, and dysmorphic features emerging as key unifying features.

evidence.reference_title: Expanding the Phenotypic Spectrum of TRAF7-Related Cardiac, Facial, and Digital Anomalies With Developmental Delay: Report of 11 New Cases and Literature Review.
evidence.snippet: In this enlarged collection, novelties include a wider range of cognitive dysfunction, with some individuals exhibiting normal development despite early psychomotor delay.

nodes.description: The craniofacial skeleton and the cardiac outflow tract both derive from neural crest, and TRAF7 is expressed there. This shared origin is the proposed reason a single gene produces a face, a heart and a skull-base tumour phenotype. It is an embryological argument supported by expression and by model-organism knockdown, not by lineage tracing in patient tissue.

evidence.reference_title: Pleiotropic role of TRAF7 in skull-base meningiomas and congenital heart disease.
evidence.snippet: Further, the shared genetics of the two disparate pathologies can be traced to the common origin of forebrain meninges and cardiac outflow tract from the TRAF7-expressing neural crest.

evidence.reference_title: De Novo Missense Variants in TRAF7 Cause Developmental Delay, Congenital Anomalies, and Dysmorphic Features.
evidence.snippet: Gene-specific mutation rate analysis showed that the occurrence of the de novo variants in TRAF7 (p = 2.6 × 10-3) and the recurrent de novo c.1964G>A (p.Arg655Gln) variant (p = 1.9 × 10-8) in our exome cohort was unlikely to have occurred by chance.

evidence.reference_title: Phenotypic spectrum and transcriptomic profile associated with germline variants in TRAF7.
evidence.snippet: Almost all variants occur in the WD40 repeats and most are recurrent.

nodes.description: Traf7-deficient mouse embryos die around midgestation from loss of endothelial integrity, with reduced Klf2 expression, phenocopying Mekk3, Mek5 and Erk5 nulls. Endothelial deletion in postnatal mice causes severe cerebral haemorrhage.

evidence.reference_title: TRAF7 is an essential regulator of blood vessel integrity during mouse embryonic and neonatal development.
evidence.snippet: Targeted deletion of TRAF7 revealed that it is a crucial part of shear stress-responsive MEKK3-MEK5-ERK5 signaling pathway induced in endothelial cells by blood flow.
